# Coastal State Reporting {#sec-flag}

## Artisanal ACE

Although Niue is not a flag state, this section presents annual catch estimates derived from artisanal
fishery data. To improve the estimate of annual production, catch landings recorded in TAILS are raised
using estimated fishing activity — the number of boats and canoes estimated to fish daily at each landing
site. Table 1 presents the raised and unraised estimates per species for 2025, and Table 2 shows the
percentage contribution of each species.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-raised-ace
#| results: 'asis'
#| tbl-cap: Raised and unraised annual artisanal catch estimates in mt

source_labels <- c(tufman2 = "Tufman2 (Tails)", ikasavea = "Ikasavea")

sources_note <- glue::glue(
  "Data sources: {paste(source_labels[artisanal_data_sources], collapse = ' + ')}.",
  if (!is.null(local_knowl_trips_file))
    " Member-estimated (local knowledge) trip counts were incorporated where higher than reported trips."
  else "No estimated trips are available per landing sites, therefore, catch values could not be raised. "
)

flextable(artisanal_ace$ace_summary|>
  mutate(Method = str_to_title(Method)))  |>
  fontsize(size = 8, part = "all") |>
  fit_to_width(max_width = 8) |>
  add_footer_lines(sources_note) |>
  fontsize(size = 7, part = "footer")
```

# Socio-economic factors

Whale watching is on the rise, with locals increasingly taking tourists out on charters during the June–
September whale migration season.
Disposal of catch
Sharks that are caught in Niue’s waters must be discarded as per Niue’s legislation and the National
Pelagic Management plan.

# Onshore developments

The processing plant remains inactive, with no immediate plans for reactivation. Most current onshore
development relates to access infrastructure, in particular the wharf upgrade. The upgrade aims to
provide easier and safer offloading for fishing vessels, given the exposed nature of Niue’s only port, an
issue identified during the last operational review as a key area for improvement. A boat and canoe
launching site on the southern side of the island has also been used to offload catch when the main port
was too rough for normal operations.

# Future prospects of the fishery

The Pelagic Development and Management Plan provides the framework for guiding current and future
prospects in the fishery, supported by long- and short-term partnerships. One key long-term partnership
is with the Niue Ocean Wide (NOW) project, which is establishing management arrangements for Niue’s
newest and largest marine protected area. The MPA will cover significant inshore and offshore habitats
and species, along with both fishing and non-fishing activities. Work with NOW is already underway
to develop surveillance tools for monitoring parts of the MPA. Negotiations regarding Niue’s High Seas
allocation are also ongoing.
Status of tuna fishery data collection systems
The process of data collection is enshrined in the Licensing terms and conditions of foreign vessels fishing
in Niue waters. Reporting and data collection is mandatory with authorised Offcers rights to set the
terms, though these are based on data requirements of SPC and WCPFC. Penalties are imposed on
denying or refusal of access to data. For Artisanal data, a data offcer has been identified and appointed
to recommence collecting of data 4 days per week. In some cases including Saturday to cover Fishing
competitions held by various Communities. In previous years fishermen were relied upon to record their
own data. Along with the offshore data, this data is entered and stored in the TUFMAN database
developed by SPC.

# Research activities covering target and non-target species

Research on pelagic species is subject to funding availability and the priorities set out in the National
Pelagic Management and Development Plan. In 2010, a wahoo tagging programme was conducted using
satellite tags and the ARGOS tracking system to study wahoo movements. In 2019, tuna and shark
tagging was carried out in collaboration with the NOW project. In 2016, Niue hosted Pristine Seas
(National Geographic) to research pelagic fish assemblages using mid-water baited remote underwater
video stations (BRUVS); at the same time, the Pacific Community conducted finfish and invertebrate
surveys with Niue Fisheries staff. Further research is expected subject to funding availability.
